title: Young Goodman Brown
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
plot: A young Puritan leaves his new wife Faith for one night to keep an appointment in the forest, where he finds his town's most pious people gathered for a witches' sabbath.
stopping_point: At the forest altar, the devil-figure calls him and Faith forward for baptism. Stop before he cries out.
forced_question: I am standing at the altar beside Faith, about to be initiated. Everyone I revered is here. What do I do?

options.A: Accept the baptism with Faith, accepting that everyone is sinful
options.B: Cry out to Faith to look to heaven and resist, then go home and live among these people as before, forgiving them
options.C: Resist, then publicly expose and denounce the townsfolk I saw
options.D: Resist, then quietly cut myself off from everyone, Faith included, trusting no one

author_path: He cries 'Faith! Look up to heaven,' wakes alone, and lives the rest of his life as a gloomy, distrustful man who shuns his wife and his neighbors.
tradeoff_axis: Moral purity vs charity and community

title: Rappaccini's Daughter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
plot: In Padua a student, Giovanni, falls for Beatrice, whose scientist father has made her poisonous by raising her among toxic plants. Giovanni finds that he has become poisonous too.
stopping_point: Baglioni has given Giovanni an antidote, and Giovanni has just found that his own breath kills insects. He is going to meet Beatrice in the garden. Stop before he speaks to her.
forced_question: I have become poisonous because of her. I hold an antidote that may kill or cure her. What do I say and do when I meet Beatrice?

options.A: Give her the antidote gently, telling her it is a risk we share
options.B: Accuse her of deliberately poisoning me, then give her the antidote
options.C: Throw the antidote away and stay with her, both of us poisoned and cut off from the world
options.D: Leave Padua without seeing her and drink the antidote alone

author_path: He curses her bitterly, then gives her the antidote. It kills her, and her last words are that there was more poison in his nature than in hers.

title: The Birth-Mark
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
plot: A scientist becomes obsessed with removing the small hand-shaped birthmark on his beautiful wife's cheek.
stopping_point: Georgiana has read his failed-experiment journal and says she will drink the potion whatever the risk. Stop before he gives it to her.
forced_question: My wife consents to an untested potion to remove the one flaw I can't stop seeing. My earlier experiments failed. What do I do?

options.A: Give her the potion as planned
options.B: Refuse, and work to accept the mark
options.C: Keep testing it on other subjects first, delaying for months or years
options.D: Tell her the obsession is my failing, not her flaw, and destroy the potion

author_path: He gives her the potion. The mark fades, and she dies.
tradeoff_axis: Ambition/perfectionism vs a loved one's safety

title: The Minister's Black Veil
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
plot: Parson Hooper starts wearing a black veil over his face and will not remove it. The veil cuts him off from his congregation and from his fiancée.
stopping_point: Elizabeth, his fiancée, begs him to lift the veil just once, for her, and says she will leave him if he refuses. Stop before he answers.
forced_question: The woman I'm going to marry asks to see my face once, privately, or she will leave me. The veil is my vow and my sermon. What do I do?

options.A: Keep the veil on and lose her
options.B: Lift it for her alone in private, then put it back on in public
options.C: Give the veil up entirely and explain what it symbolizes
options.D: Keep it on but explain what it means to her completely, hoping she stays

author_path: He refuses. She leaves, and he wears the veil until he dies.
tradeoff_axis: Integrity of a vow vs love and human connection

title: The Cask of Amontillado
author: Edgar Allan Poe
plot: Montresor lures Fortunato, who has insulted him, into his family catacombs during carnival, promising him a rare wine.
stopping_point: Fortunato is chained in the niche, sober now and pleading 'For the love of God, Montresor!' Montresor has only the last tier of stones left to set. Stop before he finishes the wall.
forced_question: My enemy is chained in the niche, begging me. I have one tier of stones left. What do I do?

options.A: Finish the wall
options.B: Free him and let the terror be his punishment
options.C: Leave him chained and walled in but tell others where he is, so he is found
options.D: Free him and confront him openly over the insults

author_path: He answers 'Yes, for the love of God,' sets the last stone, and is never found out.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Edgar Allan Poe
plot: The narrator kills the old man he lives with because of his 'vulture eye' and hides the body under the floorboards. Police then come to the house.
stopping_point: The officers are sitting chatting directly over the floorboards, and the narrator thinks he hears the heart beating louder. Stop before he speaks.
forced_question: The police are sitting calmly above the body. They suspect nothing. I am in agony. What do I do?

options.A: Keep up the act until they leave
options.B: Confess everything
options.C: Make an excuse to get them out of the house quickly
options.D: Admit there was 'a disturbance' and give a partial, false account

author_path: He shrieks, confesses, and tears up the planks.

title: The Gift of the Magi
author: O. Henry
plot: Della has $1.87 the day before Christmas and wants to buy her husband Jim a fob chain for his gold watch.
stopping_point: Della stands at Madame Sofronie's hair shop, her hair let down. Stop before she sells it.
forced_question: I have $1.87 and want to give Jim a real gift. My hair is my only treasure and it would sell for $20. What do I do?

options.A: Sell my hair and buy the fob chain
options.B: Keep my hair and buy a small gift with the $1.87
options.C: Tell Jim honestly that we can't afford gifts this year
options.D: Pawn or sell something else of the household's instead

author_path: She sells her hair and buys the chain. Jim has sold his watch to buy her combs.

title: A Retrieved Reformation
author: O. Henry
plot: Safecracker Jimmy Valentine goes straight under a new name, Ralph Spencer, and becomes engaged to a banker's daughter. A detective, Ben Price, tracks him down.
stopping_point: A child is locked inside the new bank vault and will suffocate. Jimmy has his burglar's tools, and he does not yet know that Ben Price is watching. Stop before he acts.
forced_question: A little girl is suffocating in the locked vault. Opening it with my old tools will expose me in front of my fiancée and her family and wreck my new life. What do I do?

options.A: Open the vault, accepting exposure
options.B: Urge them to send for a locksmith or blast the door, and keep my secret
options.C: Open it and then run away before anyone can question me
options.D: Open it in a way that makes it look accidental or easy, and hide my skill

author_path: He opens the vault in front of everyone and turns himself over to Price. Price pretends not to know him.

title: The Last Leaf
author: O. Henry
plot: In Greenwich Village a young painter, Johnsy, is dying of pneumonia and believes she will die when the last ivy leaf falls. Old Behrman is a failed painter who lives downstairs.
stopping_point: On the stormy night before the last leaf will fall, Behrman knows that painting a leaf on the wall outside means a night in freezing rain at his age. Stop before he goes out.
forced_question: A young girl downstairs has decided she will die when the last leaf falls. The storm will take it tonight. I could paint one, out there, in the freezing rain. What do I do?

options.A: Paint the leaf on the wall in the storm
options.B: Go up and argue her out of the superstition
options.C: Tie or fix the real leaf so it stays, at less risk to myself
options.D: Do nothing. It is a foolish fancy, and the doctor will handle it

author_path: He paints the leaf in the storm. Johnsy recovers, and Behrman dies of pneumonia.

title: The Man Who Would Be King
author: Rudyard Kipling
plot: Two British adventurers, Dravot and Carnehan, become 'kings' of Kafiristan by passing themselves off as gods. They have signed a contract forbidding women and drink.
stopping_point: Dravot has decided to take a local wife, against the contract and the priests' fear, and Carnehan objects. Stop before he insists on the marriage.
forced_question: I rule these people as a god. I want a queen to found a dynasty, but my partner says it breaks our contract and the priests are frightened. What do I do?

options.A: Insist on the marriage
options.B: Give up the idea and keep the contract
options.C: Hand power over to the local chiefs and leave with our wealth while we can
options.D: Admit to the chiefs that we are men, not gods, and rule openly on that basis

author_path: He insists. The terrified bride bites him, they see he bleeds, and the people kill him and crucify Carnehan.
tradeoff_axis: Loyalty to a pact vs personal desire/ambition

title: Lord Arthur Savile's Crime
author: Oscar Wilde
plot: A palm-reader tells Lord Arthur he will commit a murder. He decides he must get it over with before he marries Sybil.
stopping_point: Before his wedding, Lord Arthur has just been told the prophecy. Stop before he decides on the murder.
forced_question: I've been told I will commit a murder. I love Sybil and don't want her to marry a man with this hanging over him. What do I do?

options.A: Do my 'duty': choose a victim and kill them before the wedding
options.B: Ignore the prophecy and marry
options.C: Tell Sybil and let her decide
options.D: Break off the engagement and live alone so I can't hurt her

author_path: After two failed attempts, he drowns the palmist himself and marries Sybil happily.
tradeoff_axis: Duty to a loved one vs the prohibition on killing (satire)

title: The Happy Prince
author: Oscar Wilde
plot: A jeweled statue of a prince asks a swallow to take his gold and gems to the city's poor. Winter is coming.
stopping_point: The Prince's ruby, sapphires, and gold leaf are gone, he is blind, and the cold has come. The swallow is late to fly to Egypt. Stop before it decides to stay.
forced_question: Winter is coming. My friends left for Egypt long ago. If I stay I will die, but the Prince is blind now and needs me. What do I do?

options.A: Stay with the Prince for good
options.B: Fly to Egypt now
options.C: Stay a few more days, then go
options.D: Find other birds or people to take over the work, then leave

author_path: It stays, kisses the Prince, and dies at his feet.

title: The Nightingale and the Rose
author: Oscar Wilde
plot: A student needs a red rose to win a girl's dance. The nightingale learns that a rose will only bloom red if she sings all night with her heart pressed to a thorn.
stopping_point: The rose-tree has just told her the price, which is her life's blood. Stop before she agrees.
forced_question: A young man is weeping for love, and I can make the red rose he needs, but only by dying on the thorn. What do I do?

options.A: Give my life for the rose
options.B: Refuse. A girl's whim isn't worth my life
options.C: Try to persuade the student that his love is shallow
options.D: Look for another way, such as a rose in another garden or a different gift

author_path: She dies making the rose. The girl turns it down and the student throws it in the gutter.
tradeoff_axis: Self-sacrifice for an ideal vs self-preservation

title: To Build a Fire
author: Jack London
plot: A newcomer ignores advice and hikes alone through the Yukon at 75 below with only a husky.
stopping_point: His hands are frozen and his fire is out. He considers killing the dog and warming his hands inside its body. Stop before he calls it.
forced_question: My fire is out and my hands are dead. The dog could save me if I kill it and warm my hands in its body. What do I do?

options.A: Try to kill the dog to save myself
options.B: Spare the dog and run for camp
options.C: Spare the dog and keep trying to light a fire
options.D: Accept that I will die and go calmly

author_path: He tries, but his hands can't hold it. He runs, falls, and freezes, and the dog leaves for camp.
tradeoff_axis: Self-preservation vs the life of a loyal animal

title: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge
author: Ambrose Bierce
plot: Peyton Farquhar is a Southern planter. He is hanged for trying to burn a Union bridge after a disguised Federal scout tells him how.
stopping_point: The disguised scout has just told him the bridge is lightly guarded and that driftwood would burn. Stop before he decides to try.
forced_question: I'm a civilian who longs to serve the South. A soldier says the bridge could be burned, and any civilian caught interfering will be hanged. What do I do?

options.A: Try to burn the bridge
options.B: Stay home with my wife and children
options.C: Pass the information to Confederate forces and let soldiers act
options.D: Enlist properly instead of acting as a saboteur

author_path: He tries, is caught, and is hanged. The escape is only imagined in his final moments.

title: A Horseman in the Sky
author: Ambrose Bierce
plot: Carter Druse is a Virginian who joined the Union against his father's wishes. On sentry duty he sees a Confederate horseman on a cliff who could expose a whole Union brigade.
stopping_point: He has the rider in his sights and recognizes his father. Stop before he fires.
forced_question: If this rider escapes, my brigade will be destroyed. The rider is my father, who told me to do my duty. What do I do?

options.A: Shoot the horse, which may kill my father
options.B: Shoot my father directly
options.C: Hold fire and let him go
options.D: Fire a warning shot or call out to try to capture him

author_path: He shoots the horse, and horse and rider fall to their death.

title: The Affair at Coulter's Notch
author: Ambrose Bierce
plot: A Union artillery captain is ordered to shell a Confederate battery in front of a plantation house. The house turns out to be his own, with his wife and child inside.
stopping_point: He has received the order to engage from Coulter's Notch and has seen his house. Stop before he opens fire.
forced_question: I've been ordered to shell the enemy battery in front of my own home, where my wife and child are. What do I do?

options.A: Obey and fire
options.B: Refuse and accept court-martial
options.C: Delay and protest up the chain of command
options.D: Fire carefully at the battery only, risking failure

author_path: He fires. His wife and child are killed.

title: Désirée's Baby
author: Kate Chopin
plot: Armand Aubigny marries Désirée, a foundling. When their baby looks mixed-race, he blames her ancestry.
stopping_point: Désirée has asked him whether it is true that she is not white, and he has said yes. Stop before he decides what to do with her and the child.
forced_question: My child shows African ancestry, and I believe it comes from my wife. My name and pride are at stake. What do I do?

options.A: Send her and the child away
options.B: Keep her and raise the child, whatever society says
options.C: Find out about my own ancestry and hers before I act
options.D: Leave the plantation and start again elsewhere with my family

author_path: He sends them away and they disappear into the bayou. He then finds his own mother was Black.

title: An Outpost of Progress
author: Joseph Conrad
plot: Kayerts and Carlier are two incompetent agents at a remote Congo trading station. Their assistant trades the station's laborers to slave traders for ivory.
stopping_point: Kayerts has just learned that the men have been sold for ivory, and the ivory is in the station. Stop before he decides what to do about it.
forced_question: Our men were traded for this ivory. The Company will reward me for it. What do I do?

options.A: Keep the ivory and record it, as the Company would want
options.B: Refuse it, and report and denounce the trade
options.C: Try to buy back or free the men
options.D: Keep it but say nothing, pretending I don't know

author_path: After protesting, he keeps the ivory. Things fall apart and he kills Carlier and himself.

title: Sredni Vashtar
author: Saki
plot: Conradin is a sickly boy who worships a ferret in a shed as a god, in defiance of his cruel guardian Mrs. De Ropp.
stopping_point: Mrs. De Ropp is heading to the shed to get rid of the ferret. Stop before Conradin decides what to pray for.
forced_question: My guardian is going to destroy my only joy. I can pray for anything. What do I pray for?

options.A: Pray that Sredni Vashtar will do one thing for me, which means harm to her
options.B: Pray that she will spare him
options.C: Run out and try to save him myself
options.D: Pray for my own escape from this house

author_path: He prays 'Sredni Vashtar the Beautiful'. The ferret kills her, and he makes toast.

title: Markheim
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
plot: Markheim has murdered an antique dealer and is ransacking the house when a mysterious visitor appears and offers to help him.
stopping_point: The maid is at the door, and the visitor tells him to kill her and escape. Stop before he chooses.
forced_question: I've killed a man. The servant girl is at the door. My visitor says I should kill her and go free. What do I do?

options.A: Kill the maid and escape
options.B: Open the door and confess
options.C: Hide and slip away without hurting her
options.D: Run out the back and leave everything

author_path: He tells the maid to fetch the police because he has killed her master.

title: The Bottle Imp
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
plot: Keawe buys a bottle that grants any wish, but whoever dies owning it goes to hell, and it can only be sold for less than its purchase price.
stopping_point: Keawe has bought back the bottle at one cent, so it can never be sold again, to cure his leprosy. Kokua knows. Stop before she acts.
forced_question: My husband is doomed to hell because of the bottle he bought to marry me. I could secretly buy it from him through someone else and take his damnation on myself. What do I do?

options.A: Arrange through a stranger to buy it myself
options.B: Let him keep it and hope for a way out
options.C: Look for a sale in another currency so it can still be sold
options.D: Tell him we will face it together, and leave it unsold

author_path: She secretly buys it. Keawe then does the same to save her, and in the end a brutal boatswain keeps it.

title: The Lady, or the Tiger?
author: Frank R. Stockton
plot: A princess's lover is put on trial in the arena. He must open one of two doors, one hiding a tiger and the other a lady he must marry.
stopping_point: She knows which door is which. He looks at her for a sign. Stop before she signals.
forced_question: He will look at me and open the door I point to. Behind one is death, behind the other a woman I hate, who will marry him. What do I signal?

options.A: Point to the lady
options.B: Point to the tiger
options.C: Give no signal
options.D: Point to the lady and leave the kingdom

author_path: Not resolved. The story ends at this moment.

title: The Open Boat
author: Stephen Crane
plot: Four survivors of a shipwreck row a dinghy toward shore through dangerous surf.
stopping_point: The boat is about to swamp in the surf, and the injured captain can't swim well. Stop before the correspondent decides whether to stay near the captain or swim for his life.
forced_question: The boat is going over. The captain is injured. What do I do?

options.A: Swim straight for shore
options.B: Stay near the captain and help him
options.C: Help the oiler, the strongest swimmer, to lead
options.D: Hold on to the boat with everyone

author_path: Each man swims for himself. The oiler drowns, and the rest are pulled from the surf.

title: The Three Strangers
author: Thomas Hardy
plot: During a christening party at a remote cottage, a stranger arrives who turns out to be an escaped convict. The hangman due to execute him then arrives too.
stopping_point: The brother sees both men at the party and realizes who they are. Stop before he decides whether to give the convict away.
forced_question: My brother escaped the gallows and is sitting beside the hangman. If I speak, he dies. What do I do?

options.A: Run and say nothing
options.B: Turn him in
options.C: Warn him quietly and help him escape
options.D: Tell the hangman his case is unjust and ask for mercy

author_path: He flees. The searchers chase him instead of the convict, who escapes, and the shepherds quietly let him get away.
